name: The Blue Mountains
region: New South Wales, west of Sydney
tagline: A dramatic sandstone plateau of eucalyptus forest, deep valleys and cliffs, with waterfalls, the Three Sisters and a blue haze that gives the mountains their name.
highlight: The Three Sisters at sunset from Echo Point, as the valley turns blue and the cliffs glow orange.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed wilderness two hours from Sydney, with Katoomba's Three Sisters, Scenic World, Wentworth Falls, cliff walks, Leura's gardens and the Jenolan Caves.
metaDescription: A Blue Mountains travel guide: the Three Sisters at Echo Point, Scenic World, Wentworth Falls, the Grand Canyon and National Pass walks, Leura, Jenolan Caves, train from Sydney, best time and a two-day plan.
knownFor: The Three Sisters, cliff walks, waterfalls, eucalyptus forest
goodFor: Walking, viewpoints, day trips from Sydney, nature

image.alt: The Three Sisters rock formation above the forested Jamison Valley in the Blue Mountains

intro: The Blue Mountains are a plateau of sandstone cut by deep gorges, about 100 km west of Sydney. They are not high, with a maximum elevation of around 1,000 metres, but their cliffs, canyons and forest are dramatic, and the Greater Blue Mountains Area was inscribed by UNESCO in 2000 for its eucalypt diversity. The name comes from the blue haze that hangs over the valleys, caused by fine droplets of eucalyptus oil in the air, combined with the scattering of light.

The best-known sight is the Three Sisters, three sandstone pillars at Echo Point in Katoomba, which Aboriginal Dreaming stories associate with three sisters turned to stone. Beyond them lie the deep Jamison Valley and Megalong Valley, and a network of walking tracks, waterfalls and lookouts that has been used by visitors for more than a century, since the railway arrived in the 1860s.

The mountains are easy to visit from Sydney, by train in two hours, and can be seen in a day, but they deserve a night or two, with a walk, a look at the gardens and villages such as Leura, and a slower pace. They were badly affected by bushfires in 2019–20, but the forest has regenerated and most facilities have reopened.

whyVisit.intro: The Blue Mountains offer wilderness and spectacular views within easy reach of Sydney.

points.title: Superb lookouts
points.text: Echo Point and other viewpoints look over huge valleys and cliff faces.

points.title: Walking tracks
points.text: Clifftop paths, waterfall trails and steps down into the valleys, for all fitness levels.

points.title: Scenic World
points.text: The world's steepest passenger railway, a cable car and a rainforest boardwalk.

points.title: Gardens and villages
points.text: Leura and Blackheath have cafés, galleries and beautiful gardens.

points.title: Easy from Sydney
points.text: A direct train from Central Station takes about two hours.

attractionsIntro: Katoomba and Leura are the hub, with Wentworth Falls and Blackheath close by.

attractions.name: Echo Point and the Three Sisters
attractions.text: The classic lookout over the Jamison Valley and the three rock pillars, with an easy path to the Giant Stairway, which descends into the valley.
attractions.tip: Go early or late, when the light is best and crowds are fewer.

attractions.name: Scenic World

image.alt: The Scenic Railway and cable cars of Scenic World in Katoomba

attractions.text: A family-run attraction with the Scenic Railway, an old coal-mine railway that descends a 52-degree incline, a cable car over the valley and a boardwalk through the rainforest.

attractions.name: Wentworth Falls

image.file: File:Upper Wentworth Falls, NSW, Australia - Nov 2008.jpg
image.alt: The Upper Wentworth Falls tumbling over the sandstone cliff

attractions.text: A waterfall that drops in stages more than 180 metres, with walking tracks including the National Pass, a cliff-side path carved into the rock.

attractions.name: Leura
attractions.text: A pretty village with a main street of cafés and shops, gardens and the Cliff Drive.

attractions.name: Grand Canyon Walk, Blackheath
attractions.text: A beautiful track through a rainforest gorge, with ferns, moss and waterfalls, about 3 hours.

attractions.name: Jenolan Caves
attractions.text: Some of the oldest open caves in the world, with guided tours into chambers of limestone formations. About 1.5 hours from Katoomba.

thingsToDoIntro: Walking is the highlight, with plenty of options for different abilities.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the National Pass
thingsToDo.text: A famed track from Wentworth Falls, cut into the cliff in the 1900s.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the Scenic Railway
thingsToDo.text: The steepest railway in the world, with a dramatic descent.

thingsToDo.title: Take a garden visit
thingsToDo.text: Leura Gardens, Everglades and the Mount Tomah Botanic Garden.

thingsToDo.title: Try canyoning or abseiling
thingsToDo.text: Adventure companies run canyoning trips in the slot canyons.

thingsToDo.title: Watch the sunset at Echo Point
Have a Devonshire tea
thingsToDo.text: A traditional scones and tea in a mountain café.

foodIntro: The mountains' food is café-based, with local produce and cosy pubs.

foods.name: Devonshire tea
foods.text: Scones with jam and cream, served with tea, a favourite mountain treat.

foods.name: Pub meals
foods.text: Hearty pies, steaks and schnitzels in old pubs.

foods.name: Apples and cider
foods.text: Local orchards produce apples and cider.

foods.name: Modern Australian dining
foods.text: Restaurants with local produce and wine.

accommodation.intro: Stay in Katoomba or Leura for the best access, or in a lodge for a romantic weekend.

areas.name: Katoomba
areas.text: Hotels, hostels and guesthouses near the station and Echo Point.

gettingThere.intro: Katoomba is about 100 km west of Sydney, easily reached by train or car.

options.text: About 2 hours to Katoomba, with frequent services.
options.detail: Use an Opal card or contactless.

options.text: About 1 hour 30 minutes on the M4 and Great Western Highway.
options.detail: Traffic can be heavy on weekends.

gettingAround.intro: The towns are compact, and buses link the sights.

options.text: Links Katoomba, Leura and the main lookouts.
Many sights are on foot from Katoomba station.
Useful for Jenolan Caves and Blackheath.

bestTime.headline: March–May and September–November
bestTime.summary: The mountains are cooler than Sydney, with cold winters and mild summers.

seasons.text: Crisp, clear days and autumn colours.
Cold, with occasional snow and Yulefest in July.
Warm and often humid, with a risk of bushfires.

bestTime.avoid: Days of extreme fire danger in summer, when tracks close.

itinerary.title: Two days in the Blue Mountains
itinerary.intro: Katoomba's sights first, then a walk and a village.

days.title: Katoomba
days.morning: Echo Point and the Three Sisters.

days.title: Walks and Leura
days.morning: Wentworth Falls and the National Pass.

tipsIntro: A few tips make the visit smoother.
tips: Take an early train to avoid the crowds.
Wear sturdy shoes and bring water.
Check track closures and fire warnings.
Bring a jacket, since it is cooler than Sydney.
Stay a night for the sunrise and sunset.
Book Jenolan Caves tours in advance.

faq.q: Can I visit the Blue Mountains as a day trip from Sydney?
faq.a: Yes. Trains take about 2 hours each way, and it is a popular day trip.

faq.q: Why are they called the Blue Mountains?
faq.a: The eucalyptus forest releases fine oil droplets, which scatter blue light and create a haze.
The National Pass from Wentworth Falls or the Grand Canyon at Blackheath, depending on fitness and time.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: March to May and September to November.

faq.q: Were the mountains damaged by fires?
faq.a: Yes, in 2019–20, but the forest has recovered and most facilities are open.
Not for Katoomba and Leura. A car helps for Jenolan Caves and Blackheath.
